card.name: The word in after manic-episode risk
card.fires_on: Mostly the word "in" right after "mixed/manic episode" in the antidepressant bipolar-risk warning, before "patients at risk". Also weakly on similar words just before a patient group or setting.

modes.label: Bipolar warning text
modes.description: The word "in" after "precipitation of a mixed/manic episode", leading into "patients at risk for bipolar disorder".
modes.example: may increase the likelihood of precipitation of a mixed/manic episode<< in>> patients at risk for bipolar disorder. Whether

modes.label: Other "in" before a setting
modes.description: The word "in" after seizures occurring, leading into a clinical setting.
modes.example: may increase the risk of seizures occurring<< in>> other clinical settings associated with seizures. Monitor

modes.label: Scattered stray words
modes.description: Isolated words such as a name fragment or an adjective before a dose or presentation term.
modes.example: Franz<< Red>>l at the IBM TJ Watson Research Center
